title: Domain events
summary: Record what happened inside the aggregate as an immutable event, and let independent handlers react to it after the save succeeds, instead of the aggregate calling every reaction inline.
signals: a domain method (cancel, ship, approve) that calls a mailer, a notifier or another aggregate's repository directly
an aggregate's constructor or method taking three or more unrelated service dependencies just to change its own state
adding a new side effect to a business rule means editing the method that already has several unrelated ones in it
a partial failure where one side effect (inventory released, a row written) happened but a sibling one (the status change, the email) didn't

roles.Order.cancel() (before): changes state and calls every reaction inline, in one method
roles.InventoryService / Mailer / LoyaltyLedge: unrelated collaborators the aggregate must import and hold just to call them
roles.OrderCancelled (after): an immutable record of a fact that already happened — a noun, past tense, no behaviour
roles.Order.cancel() (after): changes state and records the event; calls no one
roles.EventDispatcher (after): the list of handlers per event type; runs after the aggregate is saved
roles.ReleaseInventoryHandler / SendCancellati: independent reactions, each testable alone, each addable without touching Order

stages.title: The aggregate calls its own side effects
stages.idea: cancel() releases inventory, emails the customer and appends to a loyalty ledger inline; a failing step aborts the rest, and the method can't be exercised without wiring all three collaborators.

stages.title: cancel() records a fact; handlers react to it
stages.idea: cancel() only changes state and appends an OrderCancelled event; the application service saves the order, then dispatches the recorded events to independently-registered handlers.

checks: Why does calling the mailer and the loyalty ledger directly from cancel() couple the aggregate to things that have nothing to do with its own invariants?
What is the difference between a domain event and a command, and why is OrderCancelled named in the past tense?
Why must the aggregate be saved before its events are dispatched, rather than the other way around?
If a handler throws partway through dispatch, what state is the system left in, and why does a real system need an outbox to make that reliable?
